question: Which of the reader's 13 covered cell types have open single-cell or single-nucleus RNA in GEO, CELLxGENE or the 10x public datasets, under the rule lane-pseudobulk committed in `2b9cd0a`?

minimum.cell_types_reason: The registered control is M2h's WITHIN-GENE CELL PERMUTATION: a gene's values are permuted among its own cells. With n cells a gene has n! distinct permutations, so n = 4 is the smallest n for which 4! = 24 >= 20 permutations exist and a control p at or below 0.05 is attainable AT ALL. With three or fewer cell types the registered control cannot be run, so the comparison cannot be made as registered and no reading from it would be interpretable.
minimum.genes_reason: M2h's and M2i's registered floor is min_genes = 100, carried verbatim as the endpoint's own floor. 1,000 is the STRICTER floor this lane requires, because what must be resolvable here is not whether the endpoint is positive but whether TWO READINGS OF IT AGREE, and the difference at issue is the size M2h measured (Delta MSE about +0.04, about 2% of variance). Below 1,000 genes the gene bootstrap's interval on the bulk reading alone is wide enough to contain both agreement and disagreement, so the comparison would decide nothing.
minimum.genes_clause: A gene counts toward the 1,000 only if it is in M2h's HELD-OUT population AND resolves in EVERY qualifying cell type in BOTH modalities: exactly one row for its unversioned gene_id in that cell type's bulk table (rows suffixed _PAR_Y not counted), and a row for the same gene in that cell type's pseudobulked single-nucleus matrix. No filter on expression and no filter on any measured value.
minimum.below_either: NO_SOURCE_QUALIFIES, and the lane stops without reading a value. That is a COMPLETE answer: it says the out-of-domain test cannot be made interpretable this way, so the biosample question closes without a lift.

rule_adopted_verbatim.how: every clause and both numbers are lane-pseudobulk's. MINIMUM is IMPORTED from that lane's module rather than copied, so this lane cannot drift from it, and `pb.verdict` is called beside this lane's own to show the two agree.

biosample_identity_policy: The adopted single-cell clause requires the single-cell experiment's BIOSAMPLE to be the covered cell type. Applied to an archive with no `biosample_term_name` field, that is read as biosample IDENTITY and nothing wider: the cells the candidate file holds must BE the covered cell type, not a tissue that contains it and not a related type. A whole dissociated tissue counts for a covered type that IS a tissue -- `ovary`, `testis` -- which is exactly the relation of the ENCODE `ovary` snRNA-seq experiments lane-pseudobulk itself ADMITTED, and it does NOT count for a covered type that is a cell, because selecting that cell type's annotated subset out of a tissue is the cell-composition decision the adopted rule does not license. A purified or cultured preparation of the covered cell type DOES count, because its biosample is that cell type.
term_match_policy: The adopted clause says EXACTLY, and what that word protects is stated in the rule's own `covered_set` clause: the covered set is NOT re-derived and NOT widened. It guards against admitting a cell type that is not in the thirteen; it cannot be read as a requirement that another archive spell a cell type the way ENCODE spells it, because no other archive has the field. So BOTH counts are reported and neither is hidden: `exact_label_count` admits a candidate only when the archive's own label is the IDENTICAL STRING to the covered biosample_term_name, and `same_biosample_count` also admits one whose label is a different string for the same biosample (`CD14+ Monocytes` for `CD14-positive monocyte`). The headline count of this lane is the STRICTER of the two, `exact_label_count`.
answer_means: CELL_TYPE_MINIMUM_REACHED: the adopted minimum's FIRST number, 4 cell types, is met. It is NOT the adopted rule's `QUALIFIES`, which needs BOTH numbers: the second -- 1,000 of M2h's held-out genes resolving in every qualifying cell type in both modalities -- cannot be counted without reading the matrices, which this lane does not do. The pseudobulk-against-bulk comparison becomes RUNNABLE and that is a separate registered lane, not this one.
pseudobulk_verdict_note: lane-pseudobulk's own function returns NO_SOURCE_QUALIFIES on a None gene count BY CONSTRUCTION, whatever the cell count: that is the ordered form of its rule and it is reprinted here so no reader mistakes this lane for having counted the genes. The cell-type half is what this lane settles.

Sample_title: inCAGE scRNA-seq of fresh and fixed K562 cells for comparing to PFA fixed cells (Fresh_Fixed)
Sample_growth_protocol_ch1: K562 and L1210 cells were cultured in IMDM (Thermo Fisher, 10566016) + 10% FBS (ATCC, 30-2020) + 1x penicillin/streptomycin (Thermo Fisher, 10378016) in T25 flasks (Corning). Cell lines were cultured until they reached ~80-90% confluency. For passaging, suspension cells (K562, L1210) were resuspended gently and collected into a 15 mL tube. 5 mL of 37ºC pre-warmed complete media was used to wash the flask and was added into the same 15 mL tube. Cells were centrifuged at 300g for 4 min, followed by media aspiration and resuspension in 5 mL of fresh pre-warmed complete media. Cells were counted using an automatic cell counter and 500,000 cells were seeded into 5 mL of 37ºC pre-warmed complete media in a 25cm2 flask. For encapsulation experiments, cells were washed twice with ice cold DPBS with 0.1% BSA
Sample_extract_protocol_ch1: Cells were washed twice with DPBS with 0.1% BSA, mixed at 1:1 ration and were encapsulated into CAGEs at a final concentration of 1.2e6 cells/mL in core mix. Next, the CAGE core dextran was removed using dextranase enzyme. Following this, all steps were performed on ice. First, capsules were washed three times with an ice-cold 3X SSCI buffer with 800g spins for 1 min. Fresh cells were lysed by washing with ice-cold 7.5pH TEIS with 5 min incubations on ice. Fixed cells were reverse cross-linked in CAGEs by washing the CAGEs twice with 3x SSCI + 0.01U/μL RiboLock RNAse Inhibitor (ThermoFisher, EO0381). Next, CAGEs were washed three times with 100mM Tris (pH 7.5) with 10mM EDTA, 0.1% Igepal CA-630 (Millipore Sigma, I8896-50ML), 0.1% SDS. Finally, CAGEs were resuspended in the same solution to a volume of 1 mL and 50 μL of proteinase K (NEB, P8107S) was added followed by incubation at 56ºC for 30 min. After the reverse crosslinking, CAGEs were washed three times with 3X SSCI, three times. CAGEs were imaged and washed three times with 3X SSCI and three times with HI10, packed at 800g for 1 min and stored on ice. Reverse-transcription reaction was set on ice and performed in PCR strip tubes. A standard 100μL reaction was composed out of 60.5μL of packed capsules, 2.5μL of 10μM RT poly(T) primer housing a 10nt UMI and 6nt barcode (Table S3, RT), 3μL of 10% Igepal CA-630 (Millipore Sigma, I8896-50ML), 20μL of 5X SMARTseq3 RT buffer (100mM Tris pH 8.3, 150mM NaCl, 12.5mM MgCl2, 5mM GTP, 40mM DTT), 0.5μL of 10mM dNTPs (NEB, N0447L), 2.5μL of 40U/μL Recombinant RNase Inhibitor (Takara Bio, 2313A), 1.5μL of 50μM TSO, 5μL of Maxima H- reverse transcriptase (ThermoFisher, EP0753). Reaction volumes were scaled according to the amount of capsules used and number of reactions performed. To set up the reaction, capsules, RT primer and Igepal CA-630 (Millipore Sigma, I8896-50ML) were mixed on ice in a PCR tube, with each housing a different RT barcode. Capsules were incubated on ice for 10 min to allow the RT primer to diffuse in, followed by heating at 70ºC for 5 min and cooling down on ice. Next, RT master mix, composed out of the remaining reagents was added to each tube, ensuring a thought mixing of capsules with pipetting. Tubes were incubated on ice for 5 min and the reaction was carried out at 42ºC for 90 min, followed by cycling between 50ºC and 42ºC incubation of 2 mins for 15 cycles. Reactions were left at room temperature overnight and processed the next day. After the RT reaction, capsules were washed three times with TI100 (pH 8.0), twice with TIbS (pH 8.0), three times with ice-cold TI100 (pH 8.0) with 2 min incubations on ice. Finally capsules were washed twice with TI10 (pH 8.0). Next, Capsule dU PCR was performed to carry out cDNA amplification. After the cDNA amplification, capsules were washed three times with TI100 (pH 8.0), twice with TIbS (pH 8.0), three times with TI100 (pH 8.0), twice with TI10 (pH 8.0). Washed capsules were subjected to tree rounds of split-and-pool barcoding. Following split-and-pool barcoding, capsules were split into 8 tubes and were dissolved  using 10M NaOH. DNA was purified using MinElute PCR purification kit and barcoded cDNA was eluted into 20μL of the elution buffer. Barcoded and purified DNA was amplified using PCR. After the reaction, amplified barcoded cDNA was purified using 0.8X AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter, A63881) and was eluted into a 15μL Elution Buffer.

To construct Illumina sequencing libraries, 50 ng of barcoded and amplified cDNA was fragmented, blunted and dA-tailed by mixing it with 3.5 μL of NEBNext Ultra II FS Reaction buffer (NEB), 1 μL of fully mixed NEBNext Ultra II FS Enzyme mix (NEB) and nuclease free water to a final volume of 17.5 μL. The reaction mix was vortexed for 10 s, spanned down and placed into a preheated PCR machine for incubation at 37°C for 10 min; 65°C for 30 min; hold 4°C (lid at 75ºC). Fragmented DNA was purified using 0.8X AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter, A63881) and eluted into 16μL of water. Single-stranded DNA adapter, containing Illumina’s TruSeq read 1 (Adp. TruSeq R1 FW and RV) sequences were annealed together at the final concentration of 1.5 μM by mixing 1.5 μL of forward ligation primer and reverse ligation primer (each at 100 μM) with 97 μL of nuclease-free water and heating the solution to 95°C for 2 min and cooling it at room temperature for 5 min. 16 μL of the purified fragmented DNA was mixed with 1.25 μL of 1.5 μM annealed adapters, 1.5μL of 10X T4 DNA ligase buffer, 15 μL of NEBNext Ultra II Ligation Master Mix (NEB, E7805S kit) and 0.5 μL of NEBNext Ultra II Ligation Master Enhancer (NEB, E7805S kit). The ligation reaction was carried out by incubating in the thermocycler for 15 min at 20°C (lid at 30ºC). After ligation, the reaction mix was diluted to 100 μL and was purified using AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter, A63881) with 0.8X volume ratio and eluted into 40 μL nuclease-free water. Indexing PCR was carried out by mixing purified DNA with 25 μL of 2x NEBNext® High-Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix (NEB, M0543L) and 2.5 μL of 20μM P7 binding primer, 8 sets of 2.5μL of 20μM indexing primer that houses an 8bp library index and water to 50μL. PCR cycling program: 98 °C, 2 min; 3 cycles of 98 °C, 20 s; 55 °C, 30 s; 72 °C, 20 s and 9 cycles 98 °C, 20 s; 65 °C, 30 s; 72 °C, 20 s; with a 1 min final extension at 72 °C, and 4 °C, hold at the end. Following final library indexing, DNA was double-side purified using 0.6x-0.8x SPRIselect (Beckman Coulter, B23318) magnetic beads and eluted into 15μL.
Sample_description: inCAGE scRNA-seq of fresh K562 cells for comparing to PFA fixed cells
inCAGE scRNA-seq of PFA fixed K562 cells for comparing to PFA fixed cells
Sample_data_processing: BCL sequencing files received from Illumina BaseSpace portal were converted to raw FASTQ files for each of the 4 (R1, R2, R3, R4) sequencing reads without read trimming or masking by using bcl2fastq software (Illumina, v2.20.0.422). Raw FASTQ files were processed using a custom pipeline (available at https://github.com/AllonKleinLab/paper-data/tree/master/Mazelis2025_CAGEs). In brief, sequencing reads were demultiplexed based on Read1 index sequence (stored as read3) (index used: TATGCAGT, TACTCCTT), and were filtered based on expected structure (all barcodes matching a barcode whitelist with hamming distance of 1). The demultiplexed reads were then processed using Trimmomatic (1) (with parameters: LEADING 28; SLIDINGWINDOW 4:20; MINLEN 20), followed by Poly-A length trim to 4 nt and selecting reads that are longer than MINLEN. For surviving reads, the fraction of length composed out of same base repeats (only considering > 5) was determined, rejecting reads whose fraction is greater than 0.5.

Count matrices were generated using STARsolo pipeline (2) (STAR 2.7.9a) with the with parameters (--soloFeatures Gene, GeneFull, --genomeSAsparseD 3, --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate, --outSAMattributes CB CR UR UB UY GN GX, --outFilterScoreMinOverLread 0.3, --outFilterMatchNminOverLread 0.3, --soloCBmatchWLtype 1MM_multi_Nbase_pseudocounts, --soloUMIfiltering MultiGeneUMI_CR, --soloUMIdedup 1MM_CR, --soloMultiMappers EM, --soloCellFilter EmptyDrops_CR, --quantMode TranscriptomeSAM GeneCounts) Human GRCh38.101 genome assembly was used.
Count matrices were filtered by selecting barcodes with >1000 UMIs and fraction of mitochondrial counts being below 0.4.  Different conditions were demultiplexed based on RT barcode
Supplementary files format and content: h5ad cell x genes expression matrix for different conditions

rejected.accession: e.g. GSM9550664 (ENCODE library ENCLB761BDY), GSM9964752-5 (K562 Zim3-dCas9 pooled dual-guide screen), GSE308682, GSE283574, GSE288996
rejected.why: THE SUPERVISOR EXPECTED THE LIFT TO COME FROM PERTURB-SEQ NON-TARGETING CONTROL CELLS, AND UNDER THE ADOPTED RULE IT CANNOT. A non-targeting control cell in a Perturb-seq or CRISPRi screen carries a lentivirally integrated guide vector and a Cas9, dCas9 or Zim3-dCas9 effector; that is a genetically modified biosample, which the adopted single-cell clause excludes in the same words it excludes shRNA, siRNA, CRISPR and CRISPRi RNA-seq -- 'a knockdown is not the cell type's own RNA'. This lane does not relax that clause to admit them. The K562 candidate admitted above is an unmodified, unfixed K562 culture and owes nothing to Perturb-seq.

The only CELLxGENE dataset whose tissue label is a covered cell line is 'Massively multiplex chemical transcriptomics at single-cell resolution': a chemical perturbation screen in which every arm receives a compound or a vehicle, so there is no untreated arm to admit. Finding one would mean reading the dataset's own cell annotations, which are inside a 321 MB matrix this lane does not fetch.

rejected.clause_failed: not genetically modified, not treated, or no open per-cell matrix
rejected.why: THE SUPERVISOR EXPECTED HepG2 AND THIS SWEEP DID NOT FIND IT. 689 GEO samples match HepG2 under the single-cell terms, and the ones these queries surfaced are overexpression, CRISPRi, vector-control or drug-treatment arms, or preparations of another cell type in a study that merely mentions HepG2. Three query forms were tried: the plain single-cell sample sweep, the same narrowed by `untreated OR parental OR wild-type OR 'wild type'` (24 samples, none an unmodified HepG2 single-cell library), and the same narrowed by `benchmark OR mixture OR 'cell lines' OR titration` (364 samples, none an unmodified HepG2 single-cell library). THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THESE QUERIES AND NOT ABOUT GEO: an archive listing is what is published, not what is usable, and this lane does not claim no such submission exists.

The day-0 sample of a differentiation time course is an exact label match on an unmodified H1, and its own characteristics read `treatment: BMP4+CHIR` with a treatment protocol to match, so it is a treated biosample. GEO.limit: GEO is an archive of independent submissions with no common pipeline and no common quantification, so it CANNOT be swept exhaustively the way ENCODE's typed JSON API can. geo_count_caveat: These counts are FREE-TEXT matches on ENCODE's own term string, because GEO has no biosample vocabulary to ask. `CD14-positive monocyte` therefore answers 0, since GEO submissions do not spell it that way -- and the 10x candidate admitted for THAT VERY CELL TYPE shows what a 0 here is worth: it is the absence of a string from an index, not the absence of the cell type from the open archives. A count here says how much was available to look through and nothing about what qualifies.
what_a_listing_is: An archive listing is what is PUBLISHED, not what is USABLE. No experimental data file was fetched: each candidate file's openness is an HTTP HEAD -- a status and a byte count -- and its per-gene-per-cell content is taken from the archive's own declaration of the file, not from reading it.
what_was_not_searched: GEO exhaustively: it has no assay vocabulary and no common quantification, so the negatives here are about the named queries and not about the archive

individual GEO submissions for IMR-90, SK-N-SH, hepatocyte, keratinocyte, cardiac muscle cell and astrocyte: a search count was recorded for each, no candidate was evaluated, and their absence from the count is UNSEARCHED and not a negative
dbGaP and EGA, excluded by the adopted licence clause
any matrix's gene content: the adopted minimum's 1,000-gene clause is uncounted here
wording_limit: Agreement on this endpoint licenses the modality swap FOR THIS ENDPOINT ONLY. It is never 'single-nucleus RNA equals bulk RNA', and it is never a statement about any other endpoint, any other gene set or any cell type not counted here.
no_biosample_added: This lane adds NO biosample. It works only in cell types the reader already covers, makes no AlphaGenome request and no deletion request, and touches nothing in area J, no node model and no BioForge calibration.
money: $0.00: no model request, no key, no data needing an application
bytes_fetched_note: catalogue metadata and HTTP headers only; no experimental data file was downloaded

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
